approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 49 Chapter 728
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 3318-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public service law, the public authorities law
        and the executive law, in relation to requiring electric  corpo-
        rations  and the Long Island power authority service provider to
        prioritize  restoring  services  to  police  departments,   fire
        departments,  and ambulance services, when electric services are
        interrupted"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require that  an  electric  corporation  or  the  Long
Island  Power  Authority service provider notify the local county office
of emergency management to provide for alternate power  sources  if  the
service  provider  is  unable  to  restore  power within 24 hours to any
police or fire department or ambulance service that is  registered  with
the  Department  of Homeland Security and Emergency Services and is pre-
wired with an appropriate transfer switch.
 
  Police, fire, and ambulance services are  on  the  frontlines  of  all
emergencies,  performing lifesaving, heroic work to protect New Yorkers.
However, as drafted, this bill would create an unfunded mandate on coun-
ties to provide generators to all police departments, fire  departments,
and  ambulance  services  within their municipal boundaries, and certain
requirements in this bill override standard utility priorities,  includ-
ing  the  need  to restore power to medical facilities and hospitals, or
customers who require electricity  for  medical  needs.  To  effectively
achieve  the  goals  of  the  bill, I have reached an agreement with the
Legislature to require local governments to coordinate with local  life-
saving  services  in advance of any emergency. The changes eliminate the
need for counties to provide costly generators.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Requires electric corporations to prioritize restoring services to police departments, fire departments, and ambulance services, when such services are interrupted; prohibits such corporations from charging rate payers a higher rate for extra costs incurred due to prioritizing such services; requires that police departments, fire departments, or ambulance services be registered with the division of homeland security and emergency services for emergency provisions to apply.
title: Requires electric corporations to prioritize restoring services to police departments, fire departments, and ambulance services, when such services are interrupted
